articles.title: Orange Peel
articles.summary: Fine dimpled gloss surface, like a sprayed orange peel; reflections break into tiny cells across the panel. Reads as a normal glossy paint with a slightly broken reflection; from a distance the cells blend away and it looks like regular gloss.
articles.what: Real sprayed orange peel — a dimpled gloss that breaks reflections into cells. Up close: Fine soft mottle of light and dark cells, 6-12 px, scattered with no direction, like the dimples in sprayed lacquer. It is shown on a neutral grey input, so the finish takes your colour; the cells are a shine change only. From a distance: Reads as a normal glossy paint with a slightly broken reflection; from a distance the cells blend away and it looks like regular gloss. Measured spec (average): metal 59, roughness 32, coat 20. Shine: high gloss. Metal: low. It takes the colour you give the zone.
when: Fits: gt / sports car, show car, stock car.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Orange Peel" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Pick your colour with BASE COLOR.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Whole body: peel is a car-wide shine property
Hood and roof: sun-facing panels show the broken reflection best
No effect on colour: numbers read exactly as in your design.
Any colour graphic or stripe: the peel is spec only, so graphics keep their colour
Pairs well with: any solid colour, chrome trim, matte black, gold leaf.
pitfalls: Not a textured paint colour: it changes shine only, grey here is the neutral input
Not matte or satin: it is high gloss with cells
Avoid: big dark areas in the sim, next to other loud finishes.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 59 (low metal, like carbon or subtle flake), roughness 32 (high gloss), clearcoat 20 (very strong clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: Gloss shows the paint colour as it is, so any colour works; pick the colour for contrast with the neighbouring zones, not for the finish. Avoid: big dark areas in the sim, next to other loud finishes.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: any colour graphic or stripe: the peel is spec only, so graphics keep their colour; metallic or candy pattern layers: the peel adds a real-paint feel under them
Patterns to avoid: fine matte or carbon patterns: the peel is lost beneath them
Spec overlays that work: fine flake: more sun glint on top of the peel; clearcoat gradient strips: change how glossy it is by area
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

articles.title: Peeling Clear
articles.summary: Semi-matte dark surface with hazed, crazed patches beside intact gloss islands; looks aged and failed. Reads as plain semi-matte paint with a rough, sandy, worn look; the flecks blend into an even aged dullness.
articles.what: Clearcoat failure — islands of intact gloss beside hazed, crazed patches where it let go. Up close: Shown on a neutral grey input, so it takes your colour. Fine salt-and-pepper grain: small bright glossy flecks, 2-6 px, scattered across dull hazed patches. No metal, no colour change; the white flecks are glossy islands in the shine map. From a distance: Reads as plain semi-matte paint with a rough, sandy, worn look; the flecks blend into an even aged dullness. Measured spec (average): metal 0, roughness 137, coat 124. Shine: semi-matte. Metal: none. It takes the colour you give the zone.
when: Fits: dirt late model, truck / off-road, stock car.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Peeling Clear" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Pick your colour with BASE COLOR.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood, roof, trunk: sun-facing panels fail first on real cars
Avoid bumpers if the car should look cared for
No effect on colour: numbers keep their colours but look slightly dull.
Faded or sun-bleached colour layers: match the aged story
Pairs well with: rust, matte black, dirt, chrome.
pitfalls: Not a dirty colour: it changes shine only, grey is the neutral input
Not flake: the bright flecks are gloss, not metallic sparkle
Avoid: numbers, next to other loud finishes.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 0 (non-metal paint), roughness 137 (semi-matte), clearcoat 124 (satin or weak clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: roughness and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: Gloss shows the paint colour as it is, so any colour works; pick the colour for contrast with the neighbouring zones, not for the finish. Avoid: numbers, next to other loud finishes.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: faded or sun-bleached colour layers: match the aged story; rust, patina or chipped paint graphics: strengthen the barn-find look
Patterns to avoid: carbon, chrome or showroom patterns: contradict a failed finish
Spec overlays that work: scratches or micro wear: add more aging; matte dust or grime overlay: deepen the neglect
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

articles.title: Textured Powder
articles.summary: Even grey surface covered in fine raised grit specks; satin sheen, no pattern, reads as sand-textured powder coat. Reads as your colour with a rough, sandpapery tooth; slightly lighter and busier than a flat paint, no shapes.
articles.what: Sand-texture powder coat — a dense grit of raised specks in your colour. Up close: Takes your colour; shown on grey input as a dense crumbly grit of light and dark clumps, 2-6 px, with a few smoother soft patches. Looks like sprayed sand or powder coat, not a regular pattern. From a distance: Reads as your colour with a rough, sandpapery tooth; slightly lighter and busier than a flat paint, no shapes. Measured spec (average): metal 77, roughness 113, coat 125. Shine: satin. Metal: low. It takes the colour you give the zone.
when: Fits: truck / off-road, stock car, dirt late model.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Textured Powder" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Pick your colour with BASE COLOR.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Body, bumpers and trim: tough utility look
Big flats show the grit evenly
Bold, large numbers hold; small ones need a smooth contrasting plate.
Bold graphics and stripes: grit is a calm tooth behind them
Pairs well with: any solid colour, matte black, chrome trim, white numbers.
pitfalls: Not a flat grey: grey is only the placeholder input
Not metal flake: grit is irregular crumbs, not round sparkle
Avoid: small numbers need a clean contrasting backing when this gritty finish is behind them, large flat areas can look dull.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 77 (pearl-level metal), roughness 113 (satin or eggshell), clearcoat 125 (satin or weak clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal and roughness and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: Pearl depth shows best on a clear mid-tone or deep saturated colour; a dull grey paint hides the shift. Avoid: small numbers need a clean contrasting backing when this gritty finish is behind them, large flat areas can look dull.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: bold graphics and stripes: grit is a calm tooth behind them; tonal stencil camo: texture and shapes stay separate
Patterns to avoid: fine dots, static, noise: grit on grit; carbon or weave: mush
Spec overlays that work: gloss/matte patch: smooth plates versus gritty body; scratch roughness: workshop wear
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

articles.title: Quicksilver Pool
articles.summary: Satin surface with liquid mirror islands pooling like mercury, caustic light trapped inside them. A high-contrast salt-and-pepper mix of shiny and dull in your colour; at distance it reads as mercury splatter, a loud glittering metallic mottle on a matte base.
articles.what: Mercury pooled on matte paint — liquid mirror islands with caustic light inside them. Up close: Dense scatter of bright white blobs and round droplets, 4-30 px, merging into pools in places, on a mid-grey ground with a faint diagonal crosshatch. About half the area is bright mirror islands and half is dull. Shown on a neutral grey input, so it takes your colour; the preview grey is not the. From a distance: A high-contrast salt-and-pepper mix of shiny and dull in your colour; at distance it reads as mercury splatter, a loud glittering metallic mottle on a matte base. Measured spec (average): metal 95, roughness 97, coat 83. Shine: satin. Metal: medium. It takes the colour you give the zone.
when: Best on: hero panel, body, hood.
Fits: show car, gt / sports car, open wheel.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Quicksilver Pool" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Pick your colour with BASE COLOR.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood, roof and doors: pools of 4-30 px read on wide panels
Whole car for a full liquid metal look
Hard: shiny islands break up numbers. Use thick dark outlines or a solid dark block behind them; light numbers with a black outline read best.
Thin black or white pinstripes: tidy lines over the splatter
Pairs well with: black, deep blue, chrome, matte grey.
pitfalls: Not chrome: only about half the area mirrors, the rest is dull
Not metal flake: shapes are round pools and droplets, not square chips
Avoid: numbers, next to other loud finishes.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 95 (pearl-level metal), roughness 97 (satin gloss), clearcoat 83 (satin or weak clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal and roughness and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: Pearl depth shows best on a clear mid-tone or deep saturated colour; a dull grey paint hides the shift. Avoid: numbers, next to other loud finishes.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: thin black or white pinstripes: tidy lines over the splatter; bold stripes and numbers in a dark colour: strong contrast on the shiny and dull mix
Patterns to avoid: other splatter, flake or glitter patterns: duplicate the effect; camo and crackle patterns: clash with the pool shapes
Spec overlays that work: gloss clearcoat panels: shiny shapes on a mercury-spotted car; matte band spec: stripe that kills the shine
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

articles.title: Rain Beads
articles.summary: High-gloss surface covered in fine water beads, each drop a tiny lens with a chrome highlight. A fresh wet-after-rain look: a speckled, slightly frosty sheen over the paint, with glints from the drop edges; the individual drops blur to a sparkly dew texture.
articles.what: Water beading on a waxed panel — every drop a lens with a chrome highlight. Up close: Hundreds of round droplets, roughly 10-25 px, crowded and overlapping in clumps over a smooth surface, with the brightest sparkle on drop rims. The paint stays your own colour (grey here); the beads are a shine effect only, a lighter ring against a dull gap. From a distance: A fresh wet-after-rain look: a speckled, slightly frosty sheen over the paint, with glints from the drop edges; the individual drops blur to a sparkly dew texture. Measured spec (average): metal 94, roughness 20, coat 29. Shine: high gloss. Metal: medium. It takes the colour you give the zone.
when: Fits: gt / sports car, show car, stock car.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Rain Beads" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Pick your colour with BASE COLOR.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood, roof and trunk: horizontal surfaces are where drops sit
Sides work well too, as it is a surface effect
Numbers stay readable as the colour is untouched; drop glints sparkle over them in sun, which is fine on big numbers and a bit noisy on thin ones.
Clean solid colour or a gradient: lets the droplets read without clutter
Pairs well with: any solid colour, chrome, white, black.
pitfalls: Not water-repellent texture only: the glint is real mirror-like highlights
Not glitter or flake: round rim-lit drops, not random sparks
Avoid: big dark areas in the sim, next to other loud finishes.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 94 (pearl-level metal), roughness 20 (wet mirror gloss), clearcoat 29 (very strong clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: Pearl depth shows best on a clear mid-tone or deep saturated colour; a dull grey paint hides the shift. Avoid: big dark areas in the sim, next to other loud finishes.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: clean solid colour or a gradient: lets the droplets read without clutter; subtle fades or racing stripes: wet look under the graphics
Patterns to avoid: camo, carbon or busy mosaics: bead texture is lost in it
Spec overlays that work: gloss/matte variation bands: extra depth to the wet look; fine sparkle flake: too many glints at once, use sparingly
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.
